title: Fifth comparison passes the guards while quiet speech worsens

data.title: Fifth comparison passes the guards while quiet speech worsens
paragraphs: At update 736,850, the fifth of six native development comparisons passes every frozen numerical guard. Equal-weight nine-cohort WER is 17.639%, versus 18.511% for the preserved initial model, an absolute improvement of 0.872 percentage points. Eight cohorts improve and LibriSpeech clean regresses. This checkpoint is 0.237 points worse than checkpoint 442,110 at 17.402%, so the saved summary retains step 442,110 as the provisional best eligible candidate. Selection remains unfinished until the sixth comparison completes, and the initial model remains default.

The checkpoint records 5,132,879 training-view visits during the third pass. Visits/distinct sources are Common Voice 227,585/91,123; AMI 1,706,522/76,795; CHiME-6 3,156,531/51,743; and VOiCES 42,241/513. The qualified pool still represents 2,052,751 microphone views and 220,174 distinct source utterances. Repeated views and passes are not independent utterances. Full-parameter training, the original four-domain objective weights, source balance, quiet-view confidence and exclusion of development/evaluation remain unchanged.

Noisy and age cohort WER: AMI 26.825% to 25.134% (-1.691 percentage points; saved 95% change interval [-4.634, +0.723]); CHiME-6 76.320% to 71.910% (-4.410 percentage points; saved 95% change interval [-10.455, +1.289]); Common Voice age 12.286% to 12.124% (-0.163 percentage points; saved 95% change interval [-1.892, +1.515]). All three improve relative to initial, although AMI and CHiME-6 remain worse than checkpoint three.

Clean and native WER: CMU Arctic clean 8.541% to 8.363% (-0.178 percentage points; saved 95% change interval [-1.315, +0.904]); HiFiTTS clean 7.485% to 6.944% (-0.540 percentage points; saved 95% change interval [-1.685, +0.262]); HiFiTTS native 6.464% to 5.932% (-0.532 percentage points; saved 95% change interval [-1.087, +0.000]). HiFiTTS clean has only two development readers and native only four. The native interval reaches zero exactly; neither interval establishes a strictly positive improvement across broader reader populations.

LibriSpeech and VOiCES WER: LibriSpeech clean 5.894% to 6.056% (+0.161 percentage points; saved 95% change interval [-0.686, +0.939]); LibriSpeech native 10.269% to 10.179% (-0.090 percentage points; saved 95% change interval [-1.246, +0.956]); VOiCES 12.511% to 12.105% (-0.405 percentage points; saved 95% change interval [-1.207, +0.416]). The LibriSpeech clean regression remains inside its 0.25-point guard. VOiCES is sparsely covered by 26 source utterances, 78 microphone views and 13 speakers.

The saved 10,000-draw paired cluster-bootstrap interval for candidate-minus-initial nine-cohort WER change is [-1.693, -0.099] percentage points. The aggregate interval is below zero, while every individual cohort interval includes zero. This compares checkpoint five with initial, not with checkpoint three or four. The 0.045-point improvement over checkpoint four does not establish a reliable difference between checkpoints. The bootstrap averages microphone views per source and resamples meetings, sessions or speakers; these exploratory development intervals are not adjusted for choosing among six checkpoints.

Microphone slices retain a CHiME-6 worn-microphone regression: initial WER 41.606% rises to 45.985% on 27 clips, a 4.380-point increase. This is better than checkpoint four at 48.905% but worse than checkpoint three at 42.336%. CHiME-6 array improves from initial 79.212% to 74.864%. AMI array improves from 31.859% to 31.221% and headset from 17.804% to 14.955%. VOiCES close-microphone WER rises from 11.729% to 11.990%, while its clean and far slices improve. No slice-specific uncertainty intervals were saved; these findings do not override the frozen cohort-based decision.

Quiet-speech WER rises from 31.823% to 32.744%, a 0.921-point regression on 160 views, 77 sources and 1,004 reference words. The saved 95% change interval is [-2.761, +5.367] points. The point estimate passes the 1.0-point guard by only 0.079 points and is worse than checkpoint three at 31.781% and checkpoint four at 32.146%. Both initial and checkpoint five produce zero false positives and zero inserted words on all 20 silence/noise probes. This limited probe set does not establish product-microphone performance.

The pipeline is warming GPU shapes for its final training block toward update 884,220; 147,370 optimizer updates and one fixed development comparison remain. The frozen decision will then select one candidate, and confirmation will not choose a runner-up. Both panels reuse previously evaluated populations and provide no fresh independent confirmation. The one-reader HiFiTTS clean confirmation interval and complete nine-cohort confirmation interval are undefined, not zero uncertainty. Real product-microphone validation and an independent final age test remain absent. All new checkpoints remain experimental and the preserved initial model remains default.
